Arcadia is the right Santorini hotel for travelers who want activity and options rather than seclusion — and for families, the infrastructure is real; they’ll tell you the same. Great if you like a bit of a scene; not the move if you want exclusivity and quiet. Planning a wedding at either — room blocks at Arcadia, a buyout at Epitome — is exactly what I do.

verdict.h2: Canaves wins the top of the list. Andronis wins room for room.
paras: If you only get one Santorini trip, I’d start with Canaves. Oia Suites is the best hotel I saw on the island for first-time visitors — set higher on the Caldera than most, which buys the one thing money usually can’t here, privacy — and Epitome was my favorite hotel across nine islands, with the best sunset in Greece and no age restrictions. Those are the two seats Canaves holds in my Greece Top 10, and the River Pool Suite at Oia Suites was the single best suite I saw across 38 hotels.

But Andronis makes a promise Canaves doesn’t: a water feature in every room, at every property. If the picture in your head is a plunge pool on a cave terrace at 8am, Boutique delivers it more reliably and usually a few hundred a night below Oia Suites. Andronis also owns the two specialists — Concept for the spa, Arcadia for kids and a bit of a scene. Practically, the choice usually resolves on one question: are you booking the hotel, or booking the room?

verdict.h2: A villa you never want to leave, or a hotel nobody can find?
paras: Passalacqua is the romantic answer. It feels like being a guest at an Italian family’s estate: layered rooms, gardens that fall toward the lake, and a staff that runs it like a home. If this is the once-in-a-lifetime trip and you want the most celebrated hotel in Europe, book it.

Il Sereno is the private answer. I couldn’t find a single fault when I stayed. It’s calm, adult and quietly beautiful, and because Torno is tiny and the hotel is reachable only by its guests or by boat, it never feels busy. For the money, the Grand Suite is one of the best rooms on the lake.

And if you can’t choose, don’t. The two hotels are almost directly across the water from each other. Two nights at each, with a ten-minute private boat in between, is the trip I’d book for a honeymoon. Here’s the Passalacqua + Il Sereno pairing.

il-sereno-vs-passalacqua.guide_h2: What to know before you choose

paras: Both work, for different couples. Passalacqua is for the couple who wants the full fairy tale: frescoes, gardens and a sense of occasion at every meal. Il Sereno is for the couple who wants to be left alone with a view, a great pool and a very good bed.
If the budget allows, split the trip. Two or three nights at each gives you two honeymoons in one, and the move between them is a ten-minute boat ride.

About ten minutes by private boat. Passalacqua is on the west shore in Moltrasio and Il Sereno is on the east shore in Torno, almost directly across from each other near the southern end of the lake. By road, it’s a longer drive through the town of Como.
Both are about an hour by car from Milan’s airports, which makes either one an easy first stop.
At Il Sereno, every room sees the lake, but entry rooms get a partial view, some through the trees. The Grand Suite is where it gets special, with the head-on view and a private terrace.
At Passalacqua, the Junior Suite Al Lago opens toward the water and is the room I show couples first. With only 24 rooms, it’s the hardest confirmation on the lake, so I lock those dates first.

guide.h3: What it’s like day to day
paras: At Il Sereno, the day revolves around the water: the heated pool, a private hour in the boathouse hot tub, and one of the hotel’s own Riva boats to dinner across the lake. Torno itself is a quiet village, which is the point.
At Passalacqua, the day revolves around the estate: the gardens, the pool among the umbrellas, the clay court above the water, and dinner at the villa. You may not leave the property at all.

faq: Which is better, Il Sereno or Passalacqua?

Neither is better; they’re different. Passalacqua is the romantic 18th-century villa and the lake’s most celebrated hotel. Il Sereno is the private modern hotel with lake views from every room. Choose the villa for the fairy tale and Il Sereno for privacy and design, or split your stay between them.
Is Il Sereno cheaper than Passalacqua?
Generally, yes. Il Sereno’s Grand Suite, its best room category, starts around what an entry room costs at Passalacqua. Rates change by season, so ask me for your dates.
Can you stay at both Il Sereno and Passalacqua?
Yes, and it’s the trip I recommend for honeymoons. They are about ten minutes apart by private boat. Two or three nights at each is ideal. See my Passalacqua + Il Sereno pairing.
Which is better for families?

Neither is built for young children. Il Sereno is designed for couples, and Passalacqua, with 24 rooms, feels like a private home. For a family trip on Lake Como I’d point you to the Mandarin Oriental or Grand Hotel Tremezzo.
How far are they from Milan?
Both are about an hour by car from Milan, near the southern end of the lake.

grand-hotel-tremezzo-vs-villa-d-este.description: Grand Hotel Tremezzo vs Villa d'Este, compared by a travel advisor who toured both: Lake Como's two great classic hotels, one in the middle of the lake facing Bellagio and one in Cernobbio near Como. Which suits your trip.

The other is a Renaissance estate in Cernobbio and the lake’s original grand hotel. The choice is mostly about where on the lake you want to be.

choose.h3: If you want the middle of the lake
choose.lead: An Art Nouveau hotel from 1910 in Tremezzo, facing Bellagio across the water. It’s livelier, works well for families, and puts the villas, Bellagio and Varenna a short boat ride away. The same family owns Passalacqua.

choose.h3: If you want the institution

verdict.h2: The heart of the lake, or its most famous address?
paras: Grand Hotel Tremezzo is the one I’d pick for a first trip to the lake. It sits right in the middle, where Lake Como is at its most beautiful, with Bellagio across the water and the ferries and private boats at the door. It’s lively and colorful, and it’s easy to bring children.

Villa d’Este is the one for travelers who want the history. Everyone from royalty to film stars has swum in that floating pool, and the estate itself, with its park, grottoes and courts, is at a scale no new hotel can rebuild. It’s closer to Milan, and it’s formal, which is part of the appeal.

If you’re torn, ask yourself whether you’ll spend your days exploring the lake or enjoying the hotel. Explorers should be in Tremezzo. People who want the hotel to be the destination should be at Villa d’Este.

Lake Como is long, and where you sleep shapes the trip. Tremezzo is in the central section, where the lake’s three branches meet, so Bellagio, Varenna and Villa del Balbianello are all short hops by boat.
Cernobbio is at the southern tip, ten minutes from the town of Como. You’re closer to Milan and to Como’s restaurants and shops, but the famous mid-lake villages are a longer boat ride away.

The road up the west shore from Como is narrow and winding, and it takes 45 minutes to an hour. I usually split the journey: a car from Milan to the water in Como, then about 30 minutes by private boat to the hotel’s front door. It’s a much better first hour on the lake.

Grand Hotel Tremezzo, for most families. It’s livelier, the pools are a big draw, and it’s set up for kids in a way the more formal Villa d’Este isn’t. Villa d’Este suits multigenerational trips where the grandparents set the tone.
Villa d’Este, clearly. It’s old-world in every sense, and that’s the point. Grand Hotel Tremezzo is polished but relaxed, with more color and energy around the pools.

faq: Which is better, Grand Hotel Tremezzo or Villa d'Este?

It depends on your trip. Grand Hotel Tremezzo is better for exploring the lake and for families, because it’s mid-lake facing Bellagio. Villa d’Este is better if you want history, formality and a hotel that is the destination, and it’s closer to Milan.
Do both hotels have floating pools?
Yes. Villa d’Este’s pool floating on the lake is the original and the most famous. Grand Hotel Tremezzo also has a pool floating on the lake, alongside its other pools.
Which is closer to Milan?
Villa d’Este, in Cernobbio, is about an hour from Milan. Grand Hotel Tremezzo is further up the lake, about an hour and a half by car, or a car to Como plus about 30 minutes by private boat.
Is Grand Hotel Tremezzo good for families?
Yes. It’s one of the most family-friendly of the lake’s classic hotels, with several pools and a relaxed, lively atmosphere.
Who owns Grand Hotel Tremezzo?
The De Santis family, who also opened Passalacqua in Moltrasio.

Cernobbio sits at the southern tip of the lake, ten minutes from the town of Como. Bellagio sits at the point where the lake’s three branches meet, in the middle of everything. If you plan to explore by boat, Bellagio is the better base. If you want to arrive quickly and settle into one place, Cernobbio is.

The road to Bellagio is slow, 45 minutes to an hour from Como. I usually arrange a car from Milan to the water in Como and then a private boat of about 30 minutes to the hotel. It’s the better way to arrive on Lake Como.
Both are classic grand hotels. Villa d’Este is the more formal, and the dress code at dinner is part of the experience. Villa Serbelloni feels more relaxed because the village is right outside.

They’re different enough to combine. A couple of nights at Villa d’Este after landing from Milan, then a boat up the lake to Bellagio, gives you both sides of Lake Como: the grand estate and the village.

faq: Which is better, Villa d'Este or Villa Serbelloni?

Villa d’Este is better if you want a self-contained estate and the lake’s most famous hotel, close to Milan. Villa Serbelloni is better if you want to stay in Bellagio and explore the lake by ferry and boat.
Is Villa Serbelloni in Bellagio?
Yes. Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni is at the water’s edge in Bellagio, a short walk from the village and the ferry landing.
Which is closer to Milan?
Villa d’Este, in Cernobbio, about an hour by car. Bellagio is about an hour and a half by road, or a car to Como plus about 30 minutes by private boat.
Is Bellagio too busy in summer?

The village gets crowded with day-trippers in high season. Staying at the hotel means you have a retreat, and early mornings and evenings in Bellagio are lovely. If quiet matters most, consider Villa d’Este or a hotel on a quieter shore.
Does Villa d'Este have a floating pool?
Yes. Its pool floating on the lake is the original, and the most famous on Lake Como.

verdict.h2: A scene, or a hideaway?
paras: The EDITION is the smart modern choice. It’s fresh and social, it sits in the middle of the lake where everything is close, and it costs noticeably less than the lake’s marquee names. That leaves more of your budget for the boats, villas and restaurants that make a Como trip.

Il Sereno is the romantic modern choice. I stayed this month and couldn’t find a single fault: the design, the heated pool, the private hot tub in the old boathouse, the sheets. Because Torno is tiny and the hotel is reachable only by its guests or by boat, it never feels busy.
If you want to be out exploring every day, choose the EDITION. If you want the hotel to be the reason you came, choose Il Sereno.
The EDITION is contemporary and social, the way the brand is everywhere: a lively bar, a pool with a scene, and rooms that feel fresh rather than precious.
Il Sereno is modern in a quieter way. The feel is Japanese-minimalist and warm-industrial, with glass, walnut and stone, and there’s even a listening suite. It’s designed for couples who want calm.

The EDITION is in Cadenabbia, a couple of minutes from Tremezzo and the car ferry to Bellagio, which runs about every half hour and takes ten minutes. If you want to explore the villages, it’s the better base.
Il Sereno is in Torno, near the southern end of the lake and about an hour from Milan. It’s quicker to reach, and the hotel’s own boats make dinners across the lake easy.
At the EDITION, the decision is view versus price: the garden-facing Superior rooms are the value play, and the direct lake-view rooms are worth pricing against them. There’s a suite tier above.
At Il Sereno, every room sees the lake, but entry rooms get a partial view, some through the trees. The Grand Suite is where it gets special.
The lake road from Como is slow. I usually arrange a car from Milan to the water in Como and then about 30 minutes by private boat to Cadenabbia. It’s a far better way to arrive.

faq: Which is better, the Lake Como EDITION or Il Sereno?

The EDITION is better value and better located for exploring, with a livelier atmosphere. Il Sereno is more private, quieter and more romantic, with lake views from every room. Choose by whether you want a scene or a hideaway.
Where is the Lake Como EDITION?
In Cadenabbia, in the middle of the lake on the west shore, a couple of minutes from Tremezzo and the car ferry to Bellagio.
Is the EDITION cheaper than Il Sereno?
Generally, yes. The EDITION is the best value on the lake at this level, and Il Sereno’s better rooms are priced close to the lake’s top hotels. Ask me for your dates and I’ll price both.
Which is quieter?
Il Sereno. Torno is a tiny village, and the hotel can only be reached by guests or by boat, so there are almost no day visitors.
Which is better for a honeymoon?
Il Sereno, for most couples. For an even bigger honeymoon, pair it with Passalacqua across the water. See my Passalacqua + Il Sereno pairing.
